sub_graphs.name: DAS Core Type Aliases
sub_graphs.description: Defines the core type aliases used throughout the DAS specification for indexing rows, columns, and custody groups in the extended data matrix.

invariants.text: RowIndex, ColumnIndex, and CustodyIndex are all uint64 aliases. They MUST be used consistently for type safety when referring to matrix rows, columns, and custody groups respectively.

state_variables.name: RowIndex
state_variables.description: Row identifier in the matrix of cells.

state_variables.name: ColumnIndex
state_variables.description: Column identifier in the matrix of cells.

state_variables.name: CustodyIndex
state_variables.description: Custody group identifier in the set of custody groups.

sub_graphs.name: DAS Core Constants and Configuration
sub_graphs.description: Defines the non-configurable constants, preset size parameters, and configurable custody settings that govern the DAS system geometry and sampling behavior.

invariants.text: UINT256_MAX equals uint256(2**256 - 1) and is used as an overflow guard in custody group computation.
NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS equals uint64(CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) which is 128. This defines the fixed width of the extended data matrix.
NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS is 128. This is the total number of custody groups available for node assignment.
CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT is 4. Every honest node MUST custody at least this many custody groups.
SAMPLES_PER_SLOT is 8. This is the minimum number of custody groups an honest node must sample per slot.
NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS MUST be evenly divisible by NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS to ensure uniform column distribution across custody groups. Currently 128 / 128 = 1 column per group.

state_variables.name: UINT256_MAX
state_variables.description: Maximum uint256 value, used for overflow prevention in get_custody_groups.

state_variables.name: NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS
state_variables.description: Number of columns in the extended data matrix.

state_variables.name: SAMPLES_PER_SLOT
state_variables.description: Minimum number of samples for an honest node per slot.

state_variables.name: NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS
state_variables.description: Number of custody groups available for nodes to custody.

state_variables.name: CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT
state_variables.description: Minimum number of custody groups an honest node custodies and serves samples from.

sub_graphs.name: DataColumnSidecar Container
sub_graphs.description: Defines the DataColumnSidecar container which encapsulates a single column of extended blob data along with its KZG commitments, proofs, associated block header, and an inclusion proof. This is the primary data structure distributed over the gossip network for data availability.

invariants.text: Each DataColumnSidecar index MUST correspond to a valid ColumnIndex in the range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS).
The length of column, kzg_commitments, and kzg_proofs lists MUST all be equal and MUST NOT exceed MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK.
The kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof MUST be a valid Merkle proof of depth KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH linking the kzg_commitments to the signed_block_header.

fields.name: index
fields.description: The column index this sidecar represents.

fields.name: column
fields.description: The cells for this column, one per blob in the block.

fields.name: kzg_commitments
fields.description: The KZG commitments corresponding to each blob.

fields.name: kzg_proofs
fields.description: The KZG proofs for each cell in the column.

fields.name: signed_block_header
fields.description: The signed beacon block header this column belongs to.

fields.name: kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof
fields.description: Merkle inclusion proof for the KZG commitments in the block.

sub_graphs.name: MatrixEntry Container
sub_graphs.description: Defines the MatrixEntry container, which represents a single element in the extended data matrix. Each entry contains a cell, its KZG proof, and its position (column, row) in the matrix. This is the fundamental unit for matrix computation and recovery.

invariants.text: Each MatrixEntry column_index MUST be in the range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS).
Each MatrixEntry row_index MUST be in the range [0, MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK).
The kzg_proof in a MatrixEntry MUST be valid with respect to the corresponding cell, column_index, and the KZG commitment for the blob at row_index.

fields.name: cell
fields.description: The cell data for this matrix position.

fields.name: kzg_proof
fields.description: The KZG proof for this cell.

fields.name: column_index
fields.description: Column position in the extended data matrix.

fields.name: row_index
fields.description: Row position in the extended data matrix (corresponds to blob index).

sub_graphs.name: Custody Group Selection (get_custody_groups)
sub_graphs.description: Implements the deterministic, public custody group selection algorithm. Given a node ID and a desired number of custody groups, it computes which custody groups the node is responsible for using a hash-based pseudo-random selection. The selection is stable: increasing custody_group_count extends the existing set rather than reshuffling.

invariants.text: The returned custody groups MUST contain exactly custody_group_count unique CustodyIndex values.
All returned CustodyIndex values MUST be in the range [0, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS).
The returned list MUST be sorted in ascending order.
The selection is deterministic: the same (node_id, custody_group_count) inputs MUST always produce the same output.
Increasing custody_group_count for a given node_id MUST produce a superset of the previously returned groups (monotonic extension property).

functions.name: get_custody_groups
functions.signature: def get_custody_groups(node_id: NodeID, custody_group_count: uint64) -> Sequence[CustodyIndex]
functions.description: Deterministically computes which custody groups a node with the given node_id should custody, based on hash(uint_to_bytes(current_id)) modulo NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS. Handles overflow by wrapping current_id from UINT256_MAX to 0.

parameters.name: node_id
parameters.description: The public node identifier used to seed the pseudo-random selection.

parameters.name: custody_group_count
parameters.description: The number of custody groups to select. Must be <= NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS.

functions.returns: Sequence[CustodyIndex] - a sorted list of unique custody group indices

post_conditions.text: The returned list has exactly custody_group_count elements.
All elements in the returned list are unique (no duplicates).
The returned list is sorted in ascending order.

sub_graphs.name: Column-to-Custody-Group Mapping (compute_columns_for_custody_group)
sub_graphs.description: Computes the set of column indices that belong to a given custody group. Columns are interleaved across custody groups using a stride pattern: group g gets columns {g, g + NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS, g + 2*NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS, ...}. With NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS=128 and NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS=128, each group currently maps to exactly 1 column.

invariants.text: Each column index in the returned sequence MUST be in the range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS).
The returned columns MUST be exactly columns_per_group = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS // NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS columns.

The union of compute_columns_for_custody_group(g) for all g in [0, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS) MUST equal the set of all columns [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS). Every column belongs to exactly one custody group.
Column assignment is deterministic and uses an interleaving pattern: column c belongs to custody group c % NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS.

functions.name: compute_columns_for_custody_group
functions.description: Returns the list of column indices assigned to the given custody group using an interleaving stride of NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS.

parameters.name: custody_group
parameters.description: The custody group index to look up columns for.

functions.returns: Sequence[ColumnIndex] - the column indices belonging to this custody group

post_conditions.text: Returned sequence has exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS // NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS elements.

sub_graphs.name: Matrix Computation (compute_matrix)
sub_graphs.description: Computes the full extended data matrix from a sequence of blobs. Each blob is expanded into cells and KZG proofs via compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs, producing a flattened sequence of MatrixEntry objects. The matrix has blob_count rows and NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS columns.

invariants.text: The returned matrix MUST contain exactly len(blobs) * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS entries.
For each MatrixEntry, row_index == blob_index and column_index == cell_index within that blob's expansion.
Each (row_index, column_index) pair in the returned matrix MUST be unique.

functions.name: compute_matrix
functions.description: Computes the full, flattened sequence of matrix entries from input blobs. Iterates over each blob, calls compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs to get cells and proofs, then creates a MatrixEntry for each (blob_index, cell_index) pair.

parameters.name: blobs
parameters.description: The input blobs to be extended into the data matrix.

functions.body:
def compute_matrix(blobs: Sequence[Blob]) -> Sequence[MatrixEntry]:
    """
    Return the full, flattened sequence of matrix entries.

    This helper demonstrates the relationship between blobs and the matrix of cells/proofs.
    The data structure for storing cells/proofs is implementation-dependent.
    """
    matrix = []
    for blob_index, blob in enumerate(blobs):
        cells, proofs = compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs(blob)
        for cell_index, (cell, proof) in enumerate(zip(cells, proofs)):
            matrix.append(
                MatrixEntry(
                    cell=cell,
                    kzg_proof=proof,
                    column_index=cell_index,
                    row_index=blob_index,
                )
            )
    return matrix

pre_conditions.text: Each blob in the input sequence MUST be a valid Blob that can be processed by compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs.

post_conditions.text: The output contains len(blobs) * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS MatrixEntry objects.
Every entry has a valid KZG proof for its cell at the given (row_index, column_index).

sub_graphs.name: Matrix Recovery (recover_matrix)
sub_graphs.description: Recovers the full extended data matrix from a partial set of matrix entries using erasure coding recovery. For each blob row, it collects available cells and their column indices, then calls recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs to reconstruct missing cells. Requires at least 50% of columns per row for successful recovery.

invariants.text: The output MUST contain exactly blob_count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS entries after successful recovery.
All recovered cells and proofs MUST be valid and consistent with the original KZG commitments.
Recovery requires at least 50% of columns (NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS / 2) to be present for each blob row in the partial_matrix.

functions.name: recover_matrix
functions.signature: def recover_matrix(partial_matrix: Sequence[MatrixEntry], blob_count: uint64) -> Sequence[MatrixEntry]
functions.description: Recovers the full flattened matrix from a partial matrix. For each blob index [0, blob_count), filters partial_matrix entries by row_index, extracts cell_indices and cells, then calls recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs to reconstruct all cells and proofs for that row.

parameters.name: partial_matrix
parameters.description: A partial set of matrix entries, must have >= 50% of columns per blob row.

parameters.name: blob_count
parameters.description: The number of blobs (rows) in the matrix.

functions.returns: Sequence[MatrixEntry] - the fully recovered flattened matrix
functions.body:
def recover_matrix(
    partial_matrix: Sequence[MatrixEntry], blob_count: uint64
) -> Sequence[MatrixEntry]:
    """
    Recover the full, flattened sequence of matrix entries.

    This helper demonstrates how to apply ``recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs``.
    The data structure for storing cells/proofs is implementation-dependent.
    """
    matrix = []
    for blob_index in range(blob_count):
        cell_indices = [e.column_index for e in partial_matrix if e.row_index == blob_index]
        cells = [e.cell for e in partial_matrix if e.row_index == blob_index]
        recovered_cells, recovered_proofs = recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs(cell_indices, cells)
        for cell_index, (cell, proof) in enumerate(zip(recovered_cells, recovered_proofs)):
            matrix.append(
                MatrixEntry(
                    cell=cell,
                    kzg_proof=proof,
                    column_index=cell_index,
                    row_index=blob_index,
                )
            )
    return matrix

pre_conditions.text: For each blob_index in [0, blob_count), at least 50% of columns (>= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS / 2) MUST be present in partial_matrix for that row.
All MatrixEntry objects in partial_matrix MUST have valid cells and column_index values.

post_conditions.text: The output contains exactly blob_count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS MatrixEntry objects.
Every recovered entry has a valid KZG proof.

sub_graphs.name: Custody Protocol Requirements
sub_graphs.description: Defines the behavioral requirements for node custody including mandatory custody obligations, optional extended custody, custody sampling per slot, and how sampling integrates with the custody group selection function.

invariants.text: Nodes MUST custody all columns in each of their assigned custody groups. Partial custody of a group is not permitted.
A node's custody groups are a deterministic function of (node_id, custody_group_count), computable by any party since all inputs are public.
When syncing, a node MUST backfill columns from all of its custody groups.
A node stores custodied columns for the duration of the pruning period.
A node MUST respond to peer requests for samples on custodied columns.
A node advertising custody_group_count via ENR downloads at each slot a minimum of sampling_size = max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count) custody groups.

The custody groups to custody (get_custody_groups(node_id, custody_group_count)) MUST be a subset of the groups to sample (get_custody_groups(node_id, sampling_size)), due to the monotonic extension property.
Sampling is considered successful if and only if the node manages to retrieve ALL selected columns.

state_transitions.description: Per-slot sampling: node computes groups = get_custody_groups(node_id, max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count)), expands each group to columns via compute_columns_for_custody_group, then attempts to retrieve all columns. Success requires all columns retrieved.

sub_graphs.name: Reconstruction and Cross-Seeding Protocol
sub_graphs.description: Defines the protocol for reconstructing the full data matrix when a node has obtained at least 50% of columns, and the subsequent obligation to redistribute reconstructed data to the network.

invariants.text: If a node obtains >= 50% of all columns, it SHOULD reconstruct the full data matrix via recover_matrix.
Once a node obtains a column through reconstruction, it MUST expose the new column as if it had been received over the network.
If the node is subscribed to the subnet corresponding to a reconstructed column, it MUST send the reconstructed DataColumnSidecar to its topic mesh neighbors.
If the node is NOT subscribed to the corresponding subnet, it SHOULD still expose the availability of the reconstructed DataColumnSidecar as part of the gossip emission process.
After exposing the reconstructed DataColumnSidecar to the network, the node MAY delete it if it is not part of the node's custody requirement.

pre_conditions.text: Node MUST have >= 50% of all columns (>= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS / 2 = 64 columns) to attempt reconstruction.

post_conditions.text: After reconstruction, all NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS columns are available locally.
Reconstructed columns that fall on subscribed subnets are gossiped to mesh neighbors.

state_transitions.description: Partial matrix (>= 50% columns) -> recover_matrix -> full matrix -> gossip/expose reconstructed DataColumnSidecars -> optionally prune non-custody columns.

sub_graphs.name: Extended Data Matrix Structure
sub_graphs.description: Describes the structure of the extended data matrix: blobs are extended using one-dimensional erasure coding. The matrix has up to MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK rows and exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS columns, where each row contains a blob and its erasure-coded extension.

invariants.text: The extended data matrix has a fixed width of NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS (128) columns.
The extended data matrix has a maximum height of MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK rows.
Extension uses one-dimensional erasure coding: each blob row is independently extended.

sub_graphs.name: Modified is_data_available Helper
sub_graphs.description: Fulu-modified version of the is_data_available function. Replaces the Deneb/Electra blob-based data availability check with a column-sidecar-based check. Uses retrieve_column_sidecars to obtain column sidecars for the block, then verifies each via verify_data_column_sidecar and verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs.

invariants.text: is_data_available returns True if and only if ALL column sidecars for the given block root can be retrieved AND all pass both verify_data_column_sidecar and verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs checks.
retrieve_column_sidecars is implementation-dependent and replaces the previous retrieve_blobs_and_proofs function.
The p2p network does NOT guarantee sidecar retrieval outside of MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs.
Unlike the Deneb/Electra version, the Fulu is_data_available does NOT take blob_kzg_commitments as input. It only takes the beacon_block_root.

functions.name: is_data_available
functions.description: Checks data availability for a block by retrieving and verifying all column sidecars. Modified in Fulu (EIP-7594) to use column sidecars instead of blob sidecars.

parameters.name: beacon_block_root
parameters.description: The root hash of the beacon block to check data availability for.

functions.returns: bool - True if all column sidecars are available and valid
functions.body:
def is_data_available(beacon_block_root: Root) -> bool:
    # `retrieve_column_sidecars` is implementation and context dependent, replacing
    # `retrieve_blobs_and_proofs`. For the given block root, it returns all column
    # sidecars to sample, or raises an exception if they are not available.
    # The p2p network does not guarantee sidecar retrieval outside of
    # `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` epochs.
    column_sidecars = retrieve_column_sidecars(beacon_block_root)
    return all(
        verify_data_column_sidecar(column_sidecar)
        and verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs(column_sidecar)
        for column_sidecar in column_sidecars
    )

pre_conditions.text: beacon_block_root MUST correspond to a known block whose column sidecars are within the MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS window.

post_conditions.text: Returns True only if ALL column sidecars pass both structural verification and KZG proof verification.
If retrieve_column_sidecars raises an exception (sidecars not available), the function does not return True.

sub_graphs.name: Modified on_block Handler
sub_graphs.description: Fulu-modified version of the on_block fork choice handler. The only modification from previous forks is that is_data_available is called with only the block root (hash_tree_root(block)) instead of also passing blob_kzg_commitments. All other fork choice logic remains unchanged.

invariants.text: Parent block MUST be known (block.parent_root in store.block_states).
Block MUST NOT be from the future: get_current_slot(store) >= block.slot.
Block slot MUST be later than the finalized epoch slot.
Block MUST be a descendant of the finalized block at the checkpoint finalized slot.
Data availability MUST be confirmed via is_data_available(hash_tree_root(block)) before the block is accepted. If data is not available, the block MAY be queued for later processing.
The block MUST pass state_transition validation.

functions.name: on_block
functions.signature: def on_block(store: Store, signed_block: SignedBeaconBlock) -> None
functions.description: Processes a new block for fork choice. Validates parent existence, slot timing, finality descent, data availability (modified in Fulu to use column sidecars via EIP-7594), and state transition. Updates store with the new block and state, and recomputes checkpoints.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: The fork choice store containing block states, checkpoints, and other metadata.

parameters.name: signed_block
parameters.description: The signed beacon block to process.

functions.body:
def on_block(store: Store, signed_block: SignedBeaconBlock) -> None:
    """
    Run ``on_block`` upon receiving a new block.
    """
    block = signed_block.message
    # Parent block must be known
    assert block.parent_root in store.block_states
    # Make a copy of the state to avoid mutability issues
    state = copy(store.block_states[block.parent_root])
    # Blocks cannot be in the future. If they are, their consideration must be delayed until they are in the past.
    assert get_current_slot(store) >= block.slot

    # Check that block is later than the finalized epoch slot (optimization to reduce calls to get_ancestor)
    finalized_slot = compute_start_slot_at_epoch(store.finalized_checkpoint.epoch)
    assert block.slot > finalized_slot
    # Check block is a descendant of the finalized block at the checkpoint finalized slot
    finalized_checkpoint_block = get_checkpoint_block(
        store,
        block.parent_root,
        store.finalized_checkpoint.epoch,
    )
    assert store.finalized_checkpoint.root == finalized_checkpoint_block

    # [Modified in Fulu:EIP7594]
    # Check if blob data is available
    # If not, this payload MAY be queued and subsequently considered when blob data becomes available
    assert is_data_available(hash_tree_root(block))

    # Check the block is valid and compute the post-state
    block_root = hash_tree_root(block)
    state_transition(state, signed_block, True)

    # Add new block to the store
    store.blocks[block_root] = block
    # Add new state for this block to the store
    store.block_states[block_root] = state

    record_block_timeliness(store, block_root)
    update_proposer_boost_root(store, block_root)

    # Update checkpoints in store if necessary
    update_checkpoints(store, state.current_justified_checkpoint, state.finalized_checkpoint)

    # Eagerly compute unrealized justification and finality.
    compute_pulled_up_tip(store, block_root)

pre_conditions.text: get_current_slot(store) >= block.slot (block is not from the future).
Block MUST descend from the finalized checkpoint block.
is_data_available(hash_tree_root(block)) MUST return True (column sidecars available and valid).

post_conditions.text: store.block_states[block_root] contains the post-state after state_transition.
Proposer boost root has been updated.
Checkpoints have been updated if necessary.
Unrealized justification and finality have been computed (pulled-up tip).

state_transitions.description: Store state transition: (store, signed_block) -> store' where store'.blocks and store'.block_states are extended with the new block, and checkpoints may be updated.
